newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zairean logging project launched despite war.
newsitem.headline: Zairean logging project launched despite war.

text.p: A South African-backed logging and timber operation in Zaire is to go ahead despite an ongoing rebel war in the vast and chaotic Central African country, the project financiers said on Thursday.

A consignment of equipment worth 100 million rand will be shipped from the South African port of Durban on the east coast to Zaire next week to kick-start the Black River Timber Enterprises (BRTE) project, financed by Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank (SCMB).
A Standard Bank spokesman said the war in Zaire, which has pitted the rebel forces of Laurent Kabila against ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, would not affect the project.
"It is a totally different part of the country, a long way away. (The project) is not affected by the dispute," he said.

The saw mill and logging operation is situated in the Mai-Ndombe region of north-west Zaire and will take about 18 months to set up. Once completed, the mill will export around 180,000 cubic metres of hardwood a year.
So far the main thrusts of the rapid rebel advance have been towards the north-eastern city of Kisangani and the copper-rich southern province of Shaba.

The Zairean government has given BRTE concession rights to 1.5 million acres of tropical hardwood. The firm is a newly registered company in Zaire and its holding company is the British-based Gotvil Group.
"This project represents a major thrust into Central Africa," said Johan Smit, SCMB emerging markets director.
The project is backed by the South African government, which required three environmental reports before giving its approval.
The environmental impact of the logging will be monitored every three months to assist with a replanting programme.

Smit said the project would generate foreign currency earnings for Zaire and create local jobs, while the spin-off for South Africa would be about $31 million out of equipment sourced from the country.
